html:
Jordan is a kingdom east of the Jordan River, with its capital at Amman, ruled by the Hashemite family. It became independent in 1946. The map shows it from 1945.

Its land holds the ancient city of Petra, built by the Nabataeans. After the First World War Britain carved out the Emirate of Transjordan in 1921 and gave it to Abdullah, a son of the Sharif of Mecca who had led the Arab Revolt. In 1946 he became king.

In the 1948 war Jordan's army took the West Bank and East Jerusalem, and Jordan annexed them. Abdullah was murdered in Jerusalem in 1951. His grandson Hussein reigned from 1952 to 1999. He lost the West Bank to Israel in the Six-Day War of 1967, then fought and expelled Palestinian armed groups in Black September in 1970. He made peace with Israel in 1994.

Jordan has few resources and has taken in waves of refugees: Palestinians, Iraqis and then Syrians. Abdullah II has reigned since 1999.
sum: Jordan is a kingdom east of the Jordan River, with its capital at Amman, ruled by the Hashemite family. It became independent in 1946. The map shows it from 1945.
